latin: Methaphysicus et dialecticus aeque de omnibus disputant, sed ille demonstratiue, hic probabiliter.
translation: The metaphysician and the dialectician dispute about all things equally, but the former demonstratively, the latter probably.
translation_note: 'ille' (the former) refers back to the metaphysician, 'hic' (the latter) to the dialectician; 'probabiliter' carries the technical Aristotelian sense of arguing from reputable premises (dialectic), as opposed to demonstrative syllogism (farmer1998:14833; edelheit2022:4336).
translator: original translation, drafted 2026-09-26 by WRITER-full-batch8, from Latin at farmer1998:14833

sources.text: Aristotle's Prior Analytics 1.1 and Topics 1.1, on demonstrative versus dialectical argument
sources.pico_relation: Farmer's note gives these as the classical background to the thesis, alongside the wording of Pico's own thesis 3>9

sources.text: material on this question gathered for Pico by Elia del Medigo, cited in Kieszkowski (1964), pages 52-55
sources.pico_relation: Farmer's note states this material bears on the question

doctrine: The thesis holds that the metaphysician and the dialectician dispute about all the same matters, but the metaphysician demonstratively and the dialectician only probably (farmer1998:14833). Farmer's note traces the background to Aristotle's Prior Analytics 1.1 and Topics 1.1, and to the wording of Pico's own thesis 3>9, and states that Elia del Medigo gathered material on this question for Pico, citing Kieszkowski's 1964 study, pages 52-55 (farmer1998:14863). Edelheit cites the thesis, quoting it in full, as pertinent to the terminology and practice of 'the sceptical Academy' regarding probable argument, in a discussion that also refers the reader to Rudolf Schuessler's account of the later scholastic debate on probable opinions (edelheit2022:4336).
context: Edelheit's discussion situates the thesis within a broader treatment of scepticism and probabilism in Pico's vocabulary (edelheit2022:4336).
historiography: Edelheit is the only scholar in the material opened to discuss this thesis; he quotes its Latin verbatim and treats it as evidence for Pico's engagement with the vocabulary of probable versus demonstrative argument (edelheit2022:4336; edelheit2022:4337).

quotations.text: It is worth citing, in this context, Pico's thesis 8 according to Alexander of Aphrodisias

not_established: The content of the material gathered by Elia del Medigo for Pico on this question, beyond Farmer's citation of Kieszkowski (1964), is not established by the sources consulted.

Farmer's cross-reference to '1.1' in the harvested network appears to key to Pico's thesis 1.1 (Albert the Great), but Farmer's own note wording indicates it means Aristotle's Prior Analytics 1.1 instead; treated here as the latter (farmer1998:14863).
